messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: reserved-pool-enterprise (pool-id: rp-42) GPU utilization 100% for 6m, queue length growth > 250% in 5m window. autoscaler health: ERROR: failed to create instance (quota) x3.
ryan: I'm on it. seeing sustained queue growth on rp-42, multiple tenants showing throttled responses. any customer impact reports?
anya: acme-enterprise reported elevated 429s ~ 08:12 UTC. CS pinged earlier but no official incident opened until bot.
josh: checking autoscaler logs now. tail of controller: `Error: quotaExceeded - request denied` - looks like cloud provider rejected scale up.
kevin: are there noisy neighbors? any single tenant hogging long-running jobs?
lina: acme says some batch jobs were scheduled last night, could be that. I'll DM them for job IDs.
maya: tagging infra procurement - we might be up against reserved-GPU limits for the org. need quick mitigation for customer-facing endpoints.
ryan: plan A: apply per-tenant concurrency caps to reduce queue while we sort autoscale. Plan B: evict/kill jobs that exceed runtime threshold if they're non-critical. Plan C: request emergency pool expansion from cloud (slower).
anya: agree. I'll put a temp cap on acme and a couple other big tenants. command: `rwd-admin pool cap set --pool rp-42 --tenant acme-enterprise --concurrency 4`
ops-bot: command accepted: `pool cap set` by anya. Previous concurrency: 64 -> 4.
josh: pushing a quick probe to identify long-lived sessions: `SELECT job_id, tenant, run_time_sec FROM serving.jobs WHERE pool='rp-42' ORDER BY run_time_sec DESC LIMIT 20;` results: `job_1987 (acme) 38300s, job_2102 (beta-cust) 12100s, job_2144 (research) 9800s`
kevin: job_1987 definitely suspicious (10+ hours). Any idea what it is?
lina: that's an acme nightly rerank batch. CS confirms they kicked off a very large rerank job earlier than scheduled.
ryan: okay evict policy: non-critical batch jobs > 30m should be preempted. I'll run eviction for anything > 1800s except those tagged critical=true.
anya: `rwd-admin job evict --pool rp-42 --threshold 1800 --exclude-label critical=true` queued.
ops-bot: eviction: 12 jobs scheduled, 7 on GPUs.
josh: also noticed autoscaler process threw NPE on reconciliation loop at 08:15: `NullPointerException at org.redwood.autoscale.ScalePlanner.plan(ScalePlanner.java:312)` - suspicious patch from yesterday might have introduced a race.
kevin: can we hotpatch to disable the failing code path (fall back to legacy planner)? Minimal change: set env var `USE_LEGACY_PLANNER=true` for autoscaler deployment.
ryan: yes, do that while we investigate root cause. Josh, can you coordinate a canary set of autoscaler pods with legacy planner?
josh: deploying canary now -> `kubectl set env deployment/autoscaler USE_LEGACY_PLANNER=true -n infra && kubectl rollout restart deployment/autoscaler -n infra --selector=canary=true`
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated for autoscaler (deploy/autoscaler, tag=canary).
josh: canary pods came up healthy. monitoring queue.
anya: eviction is running; we've freed 6 GPUs so far. Queue length dropped ~35% in last 2m.
ryan: acme CS: please send short update to Acme about temporary throttling and we evicted long-running batch jobs to protect other customers. Lina, can you craft a note?
lina: drafting: "We're seeing GPU capacity pressure in our reserved pool. We've temporarily limited concurrent workloads and preempted long-running non-critical batches to reduce latency. Your team may need to re-run the job; we can whitelist critical jobs if needed." sending to Acme now.
kevin: cloud quota team replied: quota increase will take ~45 minutes manual approval. Not helpful for immediate mitigation.
maya: status page update needed. severity? Customer-facing degradation for enterprise tenants -> major. I can post an interim note: "Experiencing increased latency and throttling for some enterprise reserved pools; mitigation in progress."
ryan: go ahead. include next update in 15m.
anya: monitoring shows autoscaler metrics: reconcile_failures spike at 08:15 then drop after canary up. Looks like legacy planner stabilized decision-making and prevented further failed scale attempts.
josh: canary autoscaler executed scale-up for rp-42; cloud accepted 2 GPUs (quota allowed), pool capacity now +2, utilization down to 92% and queue continues to decline.
ops-bot: incident-bot: paging oncall ryan -> acknowledged.
ryan: I'm oncall, coordinating handoff. If we need to escalate to site reliability, ping me.
kevin: I'll open a follow-up ticket to revert the risky planner change and add better null-checks. Patch snippet: ```diff
- planner.plan(requests);
+ if (planner!=null) {
+   planner.plan(requests);
+ } else {
+   log.warn("planner null, skipping")
+ }
```
anya: plus add integration test to simulate missing model metadata.
ryan: next steps: 1) keep legacy planner on for autoscaler until full fix 2) work with cloud quota team for permanent capacity +4 GPUs 3) create tenant-level guardrails to avoid single-job monopolies 4) CS follow-up with affected customers and offer rerun assistance.
lina: Acme acknowledged and asked for ETA to re-run their job. I offered manual whitelist if they confirm it's critical.
josh: autoscaler logs show no further NPEs after canary. I'll promote legacy planner to primary while we ship fix. `kubectl set env deployment/autoscaler USE_LEGACY_PLANNER=true -n infra` promoted.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout complete.
anya: metrics 08:29 UTC: queue length down 65% from peak, average response latency for enterprise routes back to SLO for most tenants. Some residual 429s for throttled tenants.
ryan: marking incident as mitigated for now. keeping thread open for postmortem items. If anything regresses, re-alert.
maya: opening postmortem ticket and assigning owners: autoscaler bug -> eng-runtime (josh+kevin), tenant fairness guards -> eng-platform (anya), customer follow-ups -> cs (lina).
kevin: will submit PR today with null-check + unit test.
lina: CS will follow up with Acme and two other customers impacted.
ryan: nice work team. reactions: :thumbsup: :coffee:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> pool rp-42 utilization decreased to 78% at 08:37 UTC after promotions and evictions. Root cause suspected autoscaler regression + tenant batch scheduling. Postmortem target: 24h."
